readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 40:1-43:27. This is a survey day. A man with a measuring rod leads Ezekiel through a vision of a new temple, and then the glory of the LORD returns. Do not worry about the measurements. Read for the return of the glory in chapter 43.
settingTheScene: In 573 BC, the twenty-fifth year of the exile and the fourteenth after Jerusalem’s fall, Ezekiel is taken in a vision to a very high mountain in Israel. A man whose appearance is like bronze, with a measuring line in his hand, shows him a great temple complex. This is the last major vision of the book. It is a temple that has never been built in this form. Interpreters differ on its meaning, but it clearly points to a restored worship in which God’s presence is central.
observation: “In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel, and set me down on a very high mountain” (40:2).
“And behold, there was a man whose appearance was like bronze, with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand” (40:3).
“Son of man, look with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I shall show you” (40:4).
“And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was coming from the east” (43:2).
“And the glory of the LORD entered the temple by the gate facing east” (43:4).
“Behold, the glory of the LORD filled the temple” (43:5).
“Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the people of Israel forever” (43:7).
“This is the law of the temple: the whole territory on the top of the mountain all around shall be most holy” (43:12).
interpretation:
The measuring of the temple takes up chapters 40 to 42, and its precision is striking. The gates, the courts, the chambers, the altar, the walls are all measured with exact detail. The temple is a perfect square, ordered and holy. The point is not the architecture but its meaning: God intends to dwell among his people in an orderly, holy relationship. The exiles lost the first temple, and this vision gave them hope that God would restore a place of worship.

The vision is a puzzle, because the dimensions do not match Solomon’s temple or the second temple that was later built. Some scholars take it as a literal temple yet to come. Others see it as a symbolic picture of God’s perfect dwelling with his people, fulfilled in Christ and the church, and consummated in the new creation. Revelation 21 describes the new Jerusalem as a cube, with no temple, “for its temple is the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb.” Whatever view is held, the vision shows that God’s dwelling is not abandoned.

The climax is in chapter 43. Ezekiel had watched the glory leave the temple through the east gate in chapters 10 and 11. Now it returns through the same gate. The sound is like the sound of many waters, and the earth shines with his glory. The prophet falls on his face. “The glory of the LORD filled the temple.” This is the answer to the question that haunted the exiles: Has God left us forever? No. The glory returns.

God says, “This is the place of my throne… where I will dwell in the midst of the people of Israel forever.” And the condition is repentance: they must no more defile his holy name. The restoration includes a call to measure the pattern and be ashamed of their iniquities.

The message for all believers is that God wants to dwell among his people. The distance caused by sin has been overcome, and his glory returns.
connection: John 1:14 says, “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory.” John 2:19-21 shows Jesus speaking of the temple of his body. 1 Corinthians 3:16-17 and Ephesians 2:19-22 call the church God’s temple, built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets with Christ as the cornerstone. Revelation 21:3 says, “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man.” Revelation 21:22 says there is no temple in the city, for the Lord God and the Lamb are its temple.
application:
Thank God that his glory is not confined to a building, and that through Christ it has returned to dwell among his people.

Think of yourself as part of a temple being built. What does it mean for your holiness and your relationships in the church?

Pray for the return of God’s manifest presence in your worship.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that his glory fills his house.
Thank Jesus, in whom his presence dwells among us.
Ask him to make you a holy temple.
